Title 
Method for Preparing Epoxy Resin

Abstract 
This invention discloses a method for preparing epoxy resin with the following steps: weigh 
bisphenol A and an 8-10% NaOH mixed solution, mix and stir until dissolved, add 
epichlorohydrin to the solution, react at 50-100°C for 2-3.5 hours, wash with water until neutral, 
dehydrate to obtain the epoxy resin product. The 8-10% NaOH mixed solution is prepared from 
NaOH solution and alkaline saturated brine, where the alkaline saturated brine is a byproduct 
from the preparation of aliphatic epoxy resin active diluents. 
This invention organically combines the production of epoxy resin active diluents and solid 
epoxy resin, fully utilizing the alkaline saturated brine containing alkali and small amounts of 
polyols generated during the preparation of aliphatic epoxy resin active diluents as one of the 
raw materials for solid epoxy resin production. This not only saves production costs for solid

polyols generated during the preparation of aliphatic epoxy resin active diluents as one of the 
raw materials for solid epoxy resin production. This not only saves production costs for solid 
epoxy resin but also improves the toughness of solid epoxy resin products. The method features 
simple process, low energy consumption, clean production, and certain economic and social 
benefits. 
 
Claims 
Claim 1 
A method for preparing epoxy resin, comprising the following steps: Weigh bisphenol A and an 
8-10% NaOH mixed solution, mix and stir until dissolved, add epichlorohydrin to the solution, 
react at 50-100°C for 2-3.5 hours, wash with water until neutral, dehydrate to obtain the epoxy 
resin product. The molar ratio of bisphenol A, epichlorohydrin, and NaOH in the 8-10% NaOH 
mixed solution is 0.3-0.5:0.4-0.6:0.5-0.7. The 8-10% NaOH mixed solution is prepared from 
NaOH solution and alkaline saturated brine, where the alkaline saturated brine is a byproduct

mixed solution is 0.3-0.5:0.4-0.6:0.5-0.7. The 8-10% NaOH mixed solution is prepared from 
NaOH solution and alkaline saturated brine, where the alkaline saturated brine is a byproduct 
from the preparation of aliphatic epoxy resin active diluents. 
Claim 2 
The method according to claim 1, characterized in that: the molar ratio of bisphenol A, 
epichlorohydrin, and NaOH in the NaOH mixed solution is 0.44:0.57:0.60, and the 8-10% NaOH 
mixed solution contains 11-12% NaCl by mass concentration. 
Claim 3 
The method according to claim 2, characterized in that: the 8-10% NaOH mixed solution is 
prepared from 32% NaOH solution, alkaline saturated brine, and tap water, with the NaOH mass 
concentration in the alkaline saturated brine being 2-10%.

Claim 4 
The method according to claim 1, characterized in that: the bisphenol A is added when the 
temperature of the 8-10% NaOH mixed solution is below 40°C, then stirred for 10-15 minutes at 
constant temperature until dissolved before adding epichlorohydrin. 
Claim 5 
The method according to claim 1 or 3, characterized in that: the epichlorohydrin is added when 
the temperature of the solution is below 40°C. 
Claim 6 
The method according to claim 1, characterized in that: the reaction after adding epichlorohydrin 
to the solution is conducted in at least three stages: 50-80°C, 0.5-1.0h; 85±5°C, 0.5-1.0h; 
95±5°C, 1.0-1.5h. 
Claim 7 
The method according to claim 1, characterized in that: the reaction after adding epichlorohydrin 
to the solution is conducted in seven stages: 57±4°C, 15min; 70±3°C, 15min; 80±3°C, 30min; 
85±3°C, 10min; 90±3°C, 10min; 95±2°C, 20min; 97±2°C, 20min. 
Claim 8

to the solution is conducted in seven stages: 57±4°C, 15min; 70±3°C, 15min; 80±3°C, 30min; 
85±3°C, 10min; 90±3°C, 10min; 95±2°C, 20min; 97±2°C, 20min. 
Claim 8 
The method according to claim 7, characterized in that: the reaction product is washed with 
water at least 3-5 times, then dehydrated first under atmospheric pressure, followed by 
dehydration under vacuum conditions of -0.095 to -0.080 MPa to obtain epoxy resin. 
Claim 9 
The method according to claim 8, characterized in that: the reaction product is washed with 
water 7 times until neutral, then subjected to atmospheric pressure and reduced pressure 
dehydration to obtain epoxy resin. 
 
Detailed Description 
Background 
This invention relates to the field of epoxy resin production, specifically to a method for 
preparing solid epoxy resin using alkaline saturated brine byproducts from aliphatic epoxy resin 
active diluent production for solid epoxy resin preparation.

Technical Solution Benefits 
The beneficial effects of this technical solution include: 
1. Resource Utilization: Organically combines the production of epoxy resin active 
diluents and solid epoxy resin, fully utilizing alkaline saturated brine containing alkali and 
small amounts of polyols generated during aliphatic epoxy resin active diluent 
preparation. 
 
2. Cost Reduction: Significantly reduces solid epoxy resin production costs. 
 
3. Performance Enhancement: Improves the toughness of solid epoxy resin products, 
with epoxy values reaching up to 0.13 eq/100g. 
 
4. Environmental Benefits: The alkaline saturated brine contains 2-10% NaOH and less 
than 2% polyols (COD approximately 800,000 mg/L). The method features simple 
process, low energy consumption, and clean production. 
 
5. Salt Recovery: Using this method, the brine concentration after epoxy resin preparation 
reaches 23-24%, close to saturation, enabling low-cost multi-effect evaporation salt

5. Salt Recovery: Using this method, the brine concentration after epoxy resin preparation 
reaches 23-24%, close to saturation, enabling low-cost multi-effect evaporation salt 
recovery and reducing environmental pressure. 
 
Preferred Embodiments 
Optimal Ratios: The preferred molar ratio of bisphenol A, epichlorohydrin, and NaOH is 
0.44:0.57:0.60, with the 8-10% NaOH mixed solution containing 11-12% NaCl by mass 
concentration. 
Temperature Control: Both bisphenol A and epichlorohydrin should be added when the 
solution temperature is below 40°C to achieve optimal epoxy values. 
Multi-stage Reaction: The reaction is conducted in multiple temperature stages to ensure high 
epoxy value and low chlorine content, with early reactions primarily involving ring-opening and 
later reactions focusing on ring-closing. 
Purification: The product should be washed 3-7 times with water until neutral, followed by

later reactions focusing on ring-closing. 
Purification: The product should be washed 3-7 times with water until neutral, followed by 
atmospheric and vacuum dehydration to achieve high transparency, high purity, with organic 
chlorine <0.0023 eq/100g and inorganic chlorine <0.0021 eq/100g. 
 
Examples

Example 1: Epoxy Resin Preparation 
Materials: 
● 198.4g saturated brine from 1,4-butanediol glycerol ether production (alkali content 
4.82%, COD 149,940 mg/L) 
● 46.7g of 32% NaOH solution 
● 100g bisphenol A 
● 52.5g epichlorohydrin 
Process: 
1. Add materials to 500ml four-neck flask with electric heating mantle, stirrer, and reflux 
condenser 
2. Dissolve bisphenol A at 40°C, then add epichlorohydrin 
3. Seven-stage reaction: 57±4°C (15min) → 70±3°C (15min) → 80±3°C (30min) → 85±3°C 
(10min) → 90±3°C (10min) → 95±2°C (20min) → 97±2°C (20min) 
4. Wash 7 times until neutral, dehydrate under atmospheric pressure, then under -0.095 
MPa vacuum 
Result: Epoxy value 0.1298 eq/100g 
Examples 2-7 
Similar procedures using different glycol ether production byproducts, achieving epoxy values 
ranging from 0.1251 to 0.1332 eq/100g. 
Example 8: Control (Without Saturated Brine) 
Using only 32% NaOH solution without saturated brine byproduct. Result: Epoxy value 0.1232

ranging from 0.1251 to 0.1332 eq/100g. 
Example 8: Control (Without Saturated Brine) 
Using only 32% NaOH solution without saturated brine byproduct. Result: Epoxy value 0.1232 
eq/100g (lower than examples using byproduct)

Standard 88-95 0.115-0.130 ≤0.02 <0.005 
Application Performance 
The prepared epoxy resin, when applied in powder coatings, shows: 
● Smooth, high-gloss surface finish 
● No shrinkage holes or pinholes 
● Forward and reverse impact strength ≥50 kg/cm² 
● No cracking during secondary bending tests 
All products meet the quality standards for commercial bisphenol A epoxy resins and can be 
widely used in various applications.
